ratio_decidendi.ratio: A court cannot direct a legislature to enact a particular law, nor can it direct an executive authority to enact subordinate legislation. It is not within the domain of the courts to inquire into whether a public policy is wise or if a better one could be evolved. A court can only interfere if the policy is absolutely capricious, not informed by reason, totally arbitrary, and offends the basic requirements of Article 14 of the Constitution.
obiter: The directions issued by the Court are in the nature of a statutory reminder from a constitutional court to the authorities for proper implementation and not to behave like emperors considering the notion that they can do what they please.
In certain matters, there can be opinions and opinions but the court is not expected to sit as an appellate authority on an opinion.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The direction contained in paragraph 19(i) of the prior judgment is invalid because it is 'not in accord with the statutory framework.' The function of the Court is to interpret the law to ensure its working is just and fair, not to legislate or create new procedural mechanisms, as this oversteps the judicial domain and violates the separation of powers.
legal_tests_applied: Separation of Powers: 'Function of this Court is not to legislate but only to interpret the law. No doubt in doing so laying down of norms is sometimes unavoidable.'

Judicial Review of Policy: 'The court can only interfere if the policy framed is absolutely capricious or not informed by reasons or totally arbitrary and founded ipse dixit offending the basic requirement of Article 14 of the Constitution.'

Fair Procedure under Right to Life: 'Just and fair procedure being part of fundamental right to life, interpretation is required to be placed on a penal provision so that its working is not unjust, unfair or unreasonable.'

Limitation on Judicial Directives: 'this Court cannot issue any direction to the legislature to make any particular kind of enactment. Under our constitutional scheme Parliament and Legislative Assemblies exercise sovereign power to enact laws and no outside power or authority can issue a direction to enact a particular piece of legislation.'
policy_considerations: The court must balance the public policy against stifling a legitimate prosecution with the need to prevent oppressive proceedings in offenses of a private nature, where the power of quashing can be exercised.
Judicial interpretation of a penal provision is necessary to ensure its 'working is not unjust, unfair or unreasonable,' thereby upholding the fundamental right to a just and fair procedure.

The court's directions should serve as a 'statutory reminder of a constitutional court to the authorities for proper implementation and not to behave like emperors considering the notion that they can do what they please.'
